mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues rising and TRANSIT stays less negative, weekday travel intensity should lift discretionary stopovers and push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks. The mechanism is active because commuting and retail trips are recovering together in the snapshot.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -20.3 to -14.6 while TRANSIT improved from -24.6 to -20.3 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain above their t-3w to t-0w levels for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility means more people are spending time away from home, which mechanically raises demand for shopping and dining trips and increases RETAIL_REC within two weeks. This should hold when RESIDENTIAL falls below its recent level.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased from 11.3 to 7.1 over the four-week snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying at or below 8 points above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM is less negative while PARKS also rebounds, the metro is absorbing more routine local outings, and those same trip bundles spill over into retail visits over the following week. The effect should show up first as a short-lag increase in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -11.0 to -10.1 and PARKS improved from -32.1 to -27.9 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS remain less negative than their prior-week values.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp jump in TRANSIT after a weak base period signals renewed access to city centers and commuter corridors, which should raise retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if transit improvement is not sustained.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points week-on-week from a sub -23 baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -22.9 to -20.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT rise of at least 2 points from a level below -23.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility remains deeply negative, households are not substituting toward outdoor leisure, and retail visits should stay suppressed because discretionary activity is not broadening beyond necessities. The effect is strongest when PARKS stays below its recent four-week average.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed negative throughout and was -27.9 in t-0w after -35.6 in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS stays below -30 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous easing in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a coordinated return to in-person activity that should spill into retail purchases in the next two weeks. The signal is interaction-driven because neither series alone is required to move by much, but both together imply broader footfall.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -18.0 to -14.6 and TRANSIT from -23.0 to -20.3 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT becoming less negative for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-winter seasonal transition, improving park use and less-negative grocery trips should precede broader discretionary shopping, creating a one-to-four-week lift in RETAIL_REC. The mechanism is seasonally conditional because it depends on warmer-weather behavior replacing homebound routines.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both improved in t-0w relative to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-four-week mean after four weeks even though PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both continue improving.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES rises, time at home is being replaced by outside-the-home activity, and retail mobility should increase within four weeks as households reallocate outings from home to stores and venues. The effect should fail if the change is only a one-week blip.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops while WORKPLACES rises for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.3 to 7.1 while WORKPLACES improved from -20.3 to -14.6 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days when RESIDENTIAL declines and WORKPLACES increases for two straight weeks.
